QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_20

question.text: In Cat III AIFs, co-investments are less common than in Cat I/II but are emerging for certain trade types. Which scenario below BEST illustrates a Cat III co-investment pattern?

answer.text: Large single-name special-situation block trade where an anchor institutional LP co-invests alongside the fund in a listed company.
Tax pass-through to limited partners under Section 115UB.

explanation.text: The Logic: The classic co-investment pattern is in Category I/II PE/VC where an anchor LP invests directly alongside the fund in an unlisted investee. For Category III, where the strategy universe is dominated by listed/derivative trades, an analogous pattern emerges in large single-name special-situation block trades — for example a sizeable listed-company position where an anchor institutional LP takes direct line-of-sight alongside the fund. The Trap: Option B (Section 115UB tax pass-through) is a Cat I/II taxation feature, unrelated to co-investment structures. Options C (quarterly NAV) and D (retail onboarding) are unrelated operational topics. Note: The cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages define co-investment facilities for Category I/II AIFs in unlisted investee companies and discuss Category III listed/special-situation investing separately; the specific listed block-trade co-investment pattern described above is not explicitly framed as a Category III co-investment in those pages. The explanation reflects general industry practice.
